what_happened: The cloud container Athena runs in was reclaimed twice (15:18 and 16:13 UTC). Long job runs had been started as untracked nohup processes, so each reclaim killed them. Jobs mx7e and jbs2 died this way. The operator closed both jobs and asked for them again. The operator also decided that long runs will from now on be session-tracked background tasks.
cause: Athena treats the container as durable and has no custody model for running jobs. Nothing records which processes belong to which job. Nothing detects that a process died with its container. Nothing resumes or requeues interrupted jobs. How a run is launched is left to whoever starts it, and an untracked nohup looks the same as a safe launch. The only protection is the operator's habit.
prevention: Make job launching go through one Athena path that registers each run as a tracked task with a heartbeat and a persisted job state. On startup, and after any container restart, Athena reconciles that registry. A job marked running with no live process is marked interrupted and requeued, or surfaced to the operator, automatically. Athena refuses or warns on runs started outside this path. Operators then never need to close and re-ask a job by hand after a reclaim.
proposed_request: Make Athena's long-running jobs survive container reclaims. (1) Launch every job run through a single tracked path that records the job id, the process and a heartbeat in the state directory. (2) On Athena start, and whenever a job's heartbeat goes stale, find jobs marked running that have no live process, mark them interrupted and requeue them for retry without operator action. (3) Refuse, or clearly warn about, a job run started outside the tracked path. (4) Show interrupted and requeued jobs in the job status output. Done when a test that kills a running job's process mid-run results in that job being detected as interrupted and requeued automatically, and it completes on the retry.
